binders: p is an arbitrary real number.
conclusions: The real conversion of the extended-valued Lp norm of the identity function x -> x with exponent p under the centered unit-parameter Gaussian measure equals ((2^(p/2) * Gamma((1+p)/2)) / Gamma(1/2))^(1/p), where both exponentiations on the right are real powers.
mathematical_definitions: eLpNorm'(f,p,mu) is defined as (integral of ||f(x)||_e^p with respect to mu)^(1/p), valued in the extended nonnegative reals.
For the real identity function, the norm in this integral is the ordinary magnitude |x|, so the quantity inside the outer power is the p-th absolute moment of the coordinate under the given measure.

gaussianReal(0,1) is the real measure selected by the centered Gaussian construction at nonnegative parameter 1; since the parameter is nonzero, its definition uses density gaussianPDF(0,1) with respect to real volume.
Gamma is the real Gamma function, and every power on the right is Real.rpow.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real p >= 1, if X denotes the real coordinate distributed according to the centered Gaussian measure with unit nonnegative parameter, then the real-valued Lp norm of X is exactly ((2^(p/2) Gamma((p+1)/2)) / Gamma(1/2))^(1/p). Equivalently at the level of the displayed definition, the real conversion of (integral |x|^p d gaussianReal(0,1)(x))^(1/p) equals that Gamma-function expression.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement applies only to real exponents p satisfying p >= 1; values p < 1, including p=0 and negative exponents, are outside its conclusion.
It concerns only the identity coordinate under the fixed centered unit-parameter Gaussian measure, not arbitrary means, scales, functions, or measures.

The left side is formed in ENNReal and then converted to Real, but the proposition contains no explicit finiteness hypothesis for eLpNorm'; the supplied definition boundary does not expose how toReal treats infinity.

The right side uses Real.rpow and divides by Gamma(1/2). The proposition does not separately assert positivity or nonzeroness of its bases and denominator; under p >= 1 these are expected analytic facts rather than encoded hypotheses.
There is no global vacuity from the hypothesis: real values p >= 1 exist. For p < 1 the implication is vacuous pointwise because its antecedent is false.
ambiguities: The body of gaussianReal delegates the nonzero-parameter case to gaussianPDF, whose definition is not included. Thus the dossier alone does not determine whether its parameter v is conventionally described as variance, standard deviation, or another scale parameter; at the fixed value v=1 this does not change the usual centered unit Gaussian interpretation.

ENNReal.toReal is shown only as composition through ENNReal.toNNReal, whose behavior at the infinite element is not unfolded, so the precise conversion convention at infinity cannot be recovered from this dossier alone.
The definition of Real.rpow is not unfolded. The right-hand bases are expected to be positive for p >= 1, but that positivity is not itself stated in the target.
